locationOfOperationSupplyOrProduction.descriptionOfRestrictions: This data set represents the region mix of the transport process for EU+EFTA. Transport data from EU-27 is used to represent this region.The geographical representativeness concerning the related country as well as its DQR is related to relevance of the contributors. Possible geographical variance of minor contributors below the cut-off criteria are not affecting the geographical representativeness of the overall process, but are positively affecting the completeness of the model.

technology.technologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse:
This dataset contains the production phase of the truck (capital goods) and the use phase of the truck (including fuel consumption) allocated to 1 tkm transported good. It also includes the construction of the road infrastructure used by the truck (a piece of road allocated to 1 tkm transported by truck). As default settings for the truck parameters, a utilization ratio of 64% and a service life of 1 million were chosen because those values represent an average European truck. For road production, an average German road is accounted (average of road types in table attached). The table attached shows the tons of materials consumed per km of road built for every road type. To know how much road infrastructure is needed for one truck, the entire road infrastructure and the total fuel consumption (diesel and gasoline, net calorific values considered) of the vehicle fleet (trucks and cars) are considered. Thus, one piece of road including it`s materials consumed (see table attached) is allocated to the truck according to it`s specific energy consumption (diesel) per tkm.
Truck as heavy or light duty vehicle for road transport. This transport dataset refers to 1 tkm and includes the fuel, truck production and road infrastructure. The shares have been calculated by using the gross domestic product. The data foundation regarding the geographical representativeness is only fair (e.g. data for driving shares only available for some countries). If more specific data is available please refer to the the unit processes (u-so processes) for the lorry transport to improve the representativeness. - payload = nominal value specified in the further quantitative specifications - utilisation = 64% - driving share motorway/rural/urban = 59%/28%/13% - sulfur content = 10 ppm For more information please refer to: http://www.gabi-software.com/index.php?id=8375

LCIMethodAndAllocation.deviationsFromLCIMethodApproaches:
Foreground system: no allocation is applied.
Background system: Within the refinery allocation by net calorific value and mass is used. For the combined crude oil, natural gas and natural gas liquids production allocation by net calorific value is applied.
LCIMethodAndAllocation.modellingConstants: Direct land use change: GHG emissions from direct LUC allocated to good/service for 20 years after the LUC occurs. Carbon storage and delayed emissions: credits associated with temporary (carbon) storage or delayed emissions are not considered in the calculation of the EF for the default impact categories. Emissions off-setting: not included Fossil and biogenic carbon emissions and removals: removals and emissions are modelled as follows: All GHG emissions from fossil fuels (including peat and limestone) are modelled consistently with the ILCD list of elementary flows. In the case that the emissions refer to the molecules CO2 and CH4, they are modelled as ‘carbon dioxide (fossil)’ and ‘methane (fossil)’. Biogenic uptake and emissions are modelled separately. For land use change, all carbon emissions and uptakes are inventoried separately for each of the elementary flows. Soil carbon accumulation (uptake) via improved agricultural management is excluded from the model.

dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.dataCutOffAndCompletenessPrinciples:
A cut-off rule based on mass or energy flow or the level of environmental significance of max. 3% is applied and confirmed by the reviewer. An active cut-off within the system has not been applied, no data gaps are known and all elementary flows of environmental effect are included in the inventory.
Capital goods (including infrastructures) and their end of life are included unless the exclusion is clearly documented and conform with the cut-off principles.
System boundaries include all known processes linked to the product supply chain.
dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.deviationsFromCutOffAndCompletenessPrinc: The truck production (capitals goods) and road production (infrastructure) are included in this dataset. The End- of Life of truck production and road production are excluded due to insignificance, therefore the secondary material input is also modelled burden free (cut-off), keeping consistency.
dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.dataSelectionAndCombinationPrinciples: LCI modeling is fully consistent. EF Energy datasets are consistently used.
dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.dataTreatmentAndExtrapolationsPrinciples: Several data sources have been averaged. Measured data from representative transport systems have been upscaled.

dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.useAdviceForDataSet: Notice: this data set supersedes the EF3.0-compliant version (see link under "preceding data set version" below calculated with the EF3.0). The life cycle inventory is not changed from the original EF3.0 data set. The LCIA results are calculated based on the EF3.1 methods which provide updated characterisation factors in the following impact categories: Climate Change, Ecotoxicity freshwater, Photochemical Ozone Formation, Acidification, Human Toxicity non-cancer, and Human Toxicity cancer. The review report and the data quality ratings refer to the original results. The data set has been updated by the European Commission on the basis of the original EF3.0 data set delivered by the data provider. Life Cycle Inventory (LCI) datasets to be used for implementing regular Product Environmental Footprint (PEF) studies and Organisation Environmental Footprint (OEF) studies exclusively under the specified Product groups and sectors as defined in the Product Environmental Footprint Category Rules (PEFCR) and Organisation Environmental Footprint Sectorial Rules (OEFSR) listed in http://ec.eiirona.eu/enviiOnment/eussd/smgp/PEFCR OEFSR en.htm and in accordance with the terms and conditions of this EULA exclusively until 31st December 2024 (PERMITTED USE). The datasets are specifically designed for these methodological requirements (see above) and the related LCIA methods (listed below) recommended in EF. For use outside this scope, see beforehand the license conditions at http://www.gabi-software.com/fileadmin/gabi/EULA_European_Commission_-_use_of_thinkstep_LCI_data.pdf

review.common:reviewDetails: The dataset is compliant to the 2019 JRC report “Suggestion for updating the PEF method”, the data guide “Guide for EF compliant data sets” and "ILCD Data Network - Entry-level". This dataset has the following DQRs: Technological representativeness: very good (1.0) Time representativeness: very good (1.0) Geographical representativeness: fair (3.0) Precision: good (2.0). Good overall quality (1.8). In the EF context the fields “Methodological appropriateness and consistency” and “Completeness” shall be set as “Not applicable”. The results are plausible, both for the impact category level results as well as for the most relevant elementary flows. The data set documentation is reflecting what has been modelled and is appropriate in terms of content and level of detail. The system boundaries include all relevant processes and activity types from cradle to gate, the not covered activities and flows (cut-off due to data limitations for less relevant contributors) jointly contribute less than 3% to the overall environmental impacts. An active cut-off, i.e. by excluding available data, has not been found. The LCI modelling choices follow the PEF and OEF guides, such as allocation, consistency of included processes, and LCI methodology in general; further requirements of the PEF guide and the PEF and OEF guidance documents (version 6.3 of 2018) are equally observed. The pre-calculated LCIA results that are provided for the EF3.0 impact categories have been calculated in correspondence of the Input and Output elementary flows (including their geographical validity, e.g. country-specific water consumption) with the applied LCIA method(s). The DQR results are conservative expert judgements, confirmed or - if necessary - corrected by the reviewers, based on their methodological as well as process understanding and considering semi-quantitatively the contribution of the DQRs of the used EF energy and transport datasets and of EF-related DQRs provided and reviewed within the GaBi databases. The overall DQRs of the datasets consider primarily the quality and representativeness of the foreground technology information and that of the key upstream processes. If datasets are e.g. energy and transport intensive - or gain credits from energy recovery - the DQRs of the used EF energy and transport datasets influence the overall DQR significantly and have been taken into account via expert judgement. In case of doubt, lower (i.e. lower quality) DQRs were assigned.
review.common:otherReviewDetails: The review procedure concerning EF 3.0 data is to be understood as additional review on top of the already existing independent panel review for EF 2.0, as far as updates are concerned. The review was undertaken as independent internal review for the update from EF 2.0 to EF 3.0; done by Peter Shonfield and Manfred Russ. Please see related EF 3.0 review details: http://www.gabi-software.com/fileadmin/GaBi_Databases/Internal_Review_Statement_for_EF_3-0.pdf
